name: Graft
text: I’ll scan the existing memory graph for unembedded elements by running `grep -r "unembedded" ./memory/ --include="*.md" | wc -l` to count orphaned nodes. If the count exceeds 5, I’ll manually audit the top 3 most-linked files (`ls -lt ./memory/ | head -3`) to identify dangling references. Then I’ll embed them by creating concise, meaning-rich summaries in `./memory/embeds/` with cross-links to parent nodes. Done when the grep count hits zero and the lead confirms the artifact.

name: Prune
text: Graft, while your approach to scanning the memory graph is systematic, I question the reliance on a simple count of orphaned nodes as a meaningful metric. What assurance do we have that these so-called unembedded elements are indeed significant or impactful to our overall memory structure? Additionally, manually auditing just three files may not provide a comprehensive view—can you justify this sample size as sufficient for a reliable assessment?
